subject: Service provider scope: telemetry handling, legal-hold carveouts & onshore fallback
messages:
From: Grace Lim <privacy@northstarhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@northstarhealth.com
Date: 2027-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood addendum questions: telemetry, legal hold, and forced transfers

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the draft addendum — we reviewed it quickly with procurement and outside counsel. A few points we need clarified before we escalate to our InfoSec review:

1) Telemetry / transient logs: the addendum calls out "telemetry necessary to operate the service" but doesn't define retention or delineate whether that telemetry is considered "service provider" data or falls under a different exception during incident response. Our legal team needs explicit limits and examples.

2) Legal hold & deletion SLA: we require an assurance that legal hold notifications pause deletion commitments, and we need the mechanism spelled out (how long Redwood can reasonably pause deletion and how you'll notify us).

3) Forced transfers / export exceptions: if Redwood must route requests through a third-party subprocessor that results in cross-border movement, we need an onshore fallback window and an escrow/onshore routing fallback plan.

I've attached our annotated addendum excerpt. Can you confirm Redwood's proposed language for each of the above? If you can share a short dataflow diagram that maps telemetry -> processors/subprocessors that would help.

Best,
Grace Lim
Senior Privacy Counsel
Northstar Health

Attachments: Northstar_addendum_annotations.pdf (pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Grace Lim <privacy@northstarhealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood addendum questions: telemetry, legal hold, and forced transfers

Hi Grace — thanks for the clear notes. Looping in Jonas and Marissa from Legal so we can propose specific contract language.

High-level responses below; we'll follow up with redlines by EOD tomorrow and a brief dataflow diagram.

1) Telemetry: Our default stance is that telemetry strictly necessary for operation (metrics, health checks, aggregated request routing telemetry) is handled as "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA and retained no longer than 30 days by default. For incident response logs (detailed traces, access logs), we treat those as operational logs that may be retained up to 90 days and can be exported to onshore processors if required by the customer. We'll propose tightened language that enumerates categories and retention windows.

2) Legal hold: We agree to pause deletion obligations if we receive a verified legal hold notice. Proposed process: customer submits legal_hold@redwood.com with the matter id; Redwood will acknowledge within 48 hours and will pause automated deletion for up to 180 days unless otherwise agreed. We will include an exception that allows for emergency disclosures required by law (with notice to the customer).

3) Forced transfers / onshore fallback: We can commit to an onshore fallback plan for critical telemetry: if a subprocessor routing would transfer data offshore in a way that raises cross-border concerns, Redwood will attempt to route to an onshore fallback within 72 hours and will provide a temporary hold/escrow option for 14 days while we stand up the fallback, subject to capacity constraints.

Attachments: proposed_addendum_redlined.docx (docx), Redwood_Dataflow_Diagram.pdf (pdf)

We will send redline suggestions shortly.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Grace Lim <privacy@northstarhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-05T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood addendum questions: telemetry, legal hold, and forced transfers

Grace / Soojin — attaching a clean set of proposed contract snippets. High-level suggestions:

- Service provider carveout language: define "telemetry" as (i) operational metrics (aggregated, non-personal), (ii) request routing metadata (timestamps, regions), and (iii) transient KV/cache identifiers. These are service provider obligations with retention windows.

- Incident response logs: classify as "operational logs" with a separate retention and transfer clause. Include an explicit notice-and-consent pattern for any external export of full request payloads.

- Legal hold: make pause-of-deletion automatic on receipt of a verified legal hold request; require customer to include matter id and POC. Limit Redwood's pause to 180 days unless extended in writing. Add a brief SLA for acknowledgment (48 hours) and for periodic status updates (every 30 days).

- Onshore fallback and escrow: propose two-tier approach — immediate routing attempt within 72 hours, and if not feasible, Redwood to trigger an onshore escrow/queue for up to 14 days while capacity is provisioned. Add a clause that capacity-based fallback is subject to Redwood's published SLA and that extraordinary costs (e.g., urgent hot-standby provisioning) will be handled via a pre-approved PO or a one-time charge.

I flagged specific sections in the redline where Northstar's suggested 30-day subprocessor notice would need to be reconciled with our vendor onboarding cadence — I'd propose 30 days for non-emergency subprocessor onboarding and 3 days for emergency security subprocessor activations with notification "as soon as practicable."

Attachment: ccpa_cpra_addendum_v1.pdf (pdf)

-Jonas
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace Lim <privacy@northstarhealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-06T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood addendum questions: telemetry, legal hold, and forced transfers

Grace — thanks for the patience. Please see our redlined addendum attached. A few legal clarifications in-line:

- We removed blanket "forced transfer" language and replaced with a narrowly scoped operational transfer clause: Redwood will not transfer customer content outside the US except as necessary to provide the service or to comply with applicable law. Where a transfer is necessary, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to route to an onshore fallback or notify Customer and obtain instruction.

- Deletion pause: we accept a pause on deletion on receipt of a verified legal hold notice. We'll include a mechanism for the customer to request a written extension beyond the 180-day default, subject to Redwood's ability to comply and any applicable retention obligations.

- Subprocessor notice: Redwood will provide notice of new subprocessors 30 days prior to onboarding for routine additions. For emergency activations (security, incident response) Redwood will notify within 72 hours and provide a summary of data types processed and retention controls.

DocuSign link to the addendum will be issued after we align on the final redline.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
VP Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_addendum_redlined.docx (docx)

From: Grace Lim <privacy@northstarhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, procurement@northstarhealth.com, counsel@brightlineconsulting.com
Date: 2027-10-08T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood addendum questions: telemetry, legal hold, and forced transfers

Marissa / team — appreciate the redline and the pragmatic approach. A few remaining asks before we proceed to DocuSign:

1) Can you make the legal hold pause explicit that it applies to both deletion and anonymization workflows? We need confirmation automated anonymization is also paused.

2) Please confirm the 72-hour emergency subprocessor notice will include contact details for the subprocessor and a short justification for activation.

3) On the onshore fallback: for our high-risk telemetry (diagnostic traces tied to PHI), can you commit to prioritized routing (i.e., customer can request priority fallback and Redwood will provision within 48 hours subject to an agreed fee schedule)? If yes, please add language and reference to pricing appendix or PO.

If you can accept the three bullets, we can sign this week. I attached our internal approval note.

Thanks,
Grace Lim
Senior Privacy Counsel
Northstar Health

Attachments: Northstar_internal_approval_note.pdf (pdf)
